items.title: Pochettino the connector: will human touch lift Manchester United?
items.author: David Hytner
items.content:
Argentinian has excelled in man-management – but will need his powers to energise new squad and impress owners

Mauricio Pochettino celebrated his 50th birthday in style. It was March 2022, he was in charge at Paris Saint-Germain and the venue was a stunning boutique hotel; the kind that many capitals have but only Paris truly . Pochettino’s family and friends were there. So were his inner coaching circle, who are basically family. There were lots of people from PSG. And a good time was had by all.

For Pochettino, it was emotional. As everybody knows, the new Manchester United head coach is the kind of guy to well up when the speeches start, so imagine how he felt when he looked up at the big screen and a video montage of well-wishers started to roll.

items.title: Mauricio Pochettino demands say on all big first-team decisions at Manchester United
items.author: Will Unwin
items.content:
• Head coach wants control recent predecessors lacked

  • Berrada says some fan criticism ‘does cross the line’

Mauricio Pochettino has told the Manchester United hierarchy he wants a say in all major decisions related to the first team. The club’s transfer business in recent years has received plenty of criticism and the new head coach is eager for a level of control not enjoyed by his recent predecessors.

Pochettino has been given the title of head coach rather than manager but has made plain the power he is seeking, working alongside the director of football, Jason Wilcox, who is in overall charge of player recruitment.

items.title: Drone operator sorry for filming Pochettino’s first Manchester United training session
items.author: Reuters
items.content:
• Operator removes video from his channel

  • ‘I fully accept it was unethical,’ he says

A drone operator who filmed Mauricio Pochettino’s first ⁠Manchester United training ⁠session on Thursday has apologised for what he called a “total error of judgment” and removed ⁠the footage from ⁠his ​YouTube channel.

The footage was uploaded online under the username “CC OVERVIEW”. In a statement posted on his YouTube channel ⁠on Friday, the drone operator said that while the flight ​was legal under drone regulations, ‌filming the session ‌had been “unethical”.

items.title: Premier League: 10 things to look out for this weekend
items.author: Guardian sport
items.content:
Bruno Guimarães to feel the heat on Tyneside, Alex Scott’s return further cheers Cherries and Manchester City face favourite whipping boys

After three Premier League defeats on the spin, Manchester City need something or someone to come along and put some pep in their step, and Fulham look like just the thing – after all, in the past 15 years these teams have played 20 times in all competitions, and City have won precisely 20 of those games. Their current run of 17 successive league wins against Fulham is the longest run of victories by one club against a single opponent in English top-flight history. It is a reflection of the changing realities of English football, and the gulf that has opened between the teams that dominate it and those who seek to challenge them, that of the top 10 such runs all but one occurred in whole or in part after 2010 and six of them have been achieved by Sheikh Mansour’s Manchester City, with Chelsea responsible for another two, Manchester United one, and Portsmouth’s postwar, 13-game supremacy over Everton – a wild ride that included two 5-0s, a 5-1, a 6-3 and a 7-0 – the anomaly.

Manchester City v Fulham, Saturday 12.30pm (all times GMT)

Aston Villa v Sunderland, Saturday 3pm

Bournemouth v Nottingham Forest, Saturday 3pm

Coventry v Crystal Palace, Saturday 3pm

items.title: ‘Should Manchester United fans be hoping for relegation?’ Will Unwin answered your questions
items.author: Will Unwin and Guardian moderators
items.content:
As Mauricio Pochettino prepares for his first game in charge at Anfield, the Guardian’s Will Unwin answered your questions on Manchester United’s new head coach, the boardroom, the academy and whether Frank Ilett will ever get a haircut.

Every few months there is the report of a new “wonderkid” being signed: a South American full-back, a Scandinavian midfielder, a flying winger etc. But then they never seem to make the squad, let alone the first team. The same for our academy, which wins trophies regularly. Are there real prospects who could supplement or even improve the team? Is it too difficult to introduce them into Premier League games? Are they just investments for future sell-on? And why did JJ Gabriel leave?

The simple answer for many, and we can take the Paraguayan left-back Diego León as our example here, is that they are plainly not good enough and signing them has been poor . Some will take time, Sekou Kone was brought in from Mali and is out on loan at Lausanne to gain experience. Developing footballers is not an exact science and bringing them in from all around the world is a complex process to begin with. It is reliant on human factors outside football, of whether they can quickly adapt to life in a new country before even thinking about what they do on the pitch.

Continue reading...

items.title: Mauricio Pochettino calls for Manchester United to show no fear against Liverpool
items.author: Will Unwin
items.content:
• New head coach’s first game is at Anfield on Sunday

  • ‘We are going there with the idea to win and be brave’

Mauricio Pochettino has called on Manchester United to have “no fear” when they travel to Anfield on Sunday for his first game. The Argentinian does not want his players to take a backward step as he targets a fast start.

United are 18th in the Premier League and Liverpool fourth but the head coach will not accept any self-doubt. Pochettino is known for being attack-minded and is keen to instil those ideals, but will have had only three days with the players since replacing Michael Carrick.

items.title: Manchester United’s infamous 1974 relegation is a warning from history
items.author: Sam Cunningham
items.content:
It may have been a different era, but the 1970s contain salutary lessons for a club in serious decline once again

In many ways, there are striking parallels between the Manchester United relegated in 1974 and the Manchester United sitting in the relegation zone at this stage of the season for the first time in 40 years. A legendary manager leaves, his shadow remains; with boardroom dithering and uncertainty, his replacements churn and burn as the club slide over several years.

Sir Matt Busby stepped aside as manager of the 1968 European Cup-winning side, but stayed on as a director, just as Sir Alex Ferguson did, watching from the Old Trafford directors’ box as successors tried and failed.

items.title: ‘An honour’: Pochettino up for challenge of leading Manchester United revival
items.author: Will Unwin
items.content:
• New head coach faces tough opening match at Anfield

  • ‘It’s a big challenge but at the same time it’s adrenaline’

Pochettino flew from Cincinnati to Manchester overnight after overseeing the USA beating Haiti in his final game in charge. Members of Pochettino’s staff landed earlier in the week to begin work at Carrington, laying the foundations as United seek to turn their season around. His right-hand man, Jesús Pérez, the goalkeeping coach Toni Jiménez and the fitness coach Sebastiano Pochettino, who continues to work with his father, have already taken training with those not on international duty.

items.title: Mauricio Pochettino’s USMNT time will be remembered fondly, but it wasn’t transformational
items.author: Leander Schaerlaeckens
items.content:
The incoming Manchester United manager improved the US team’s culture and competitiveness, but could not bring about sea change in two years

In a theater high up in a midtown Manhattan skyscraper built from lots of glass, a highlight reel played to deafening music. And then, on “a monumental day for US Soccer”, federation president, Cindy Parlow Cone, announced they had bagged their man, Mauricio Pochettino, to become the highest-profile United States manager in the men’s national team’s history.

Pochettino held court for three-quarters of an hour in his signature blend of Spanglish before the assembled media and a grab bag of sponsors. Then he recorded some TV hits. And after that, in a bit of accidental prescience, he went off to record a podcast with Gary Neville.

items.title: Football Daily | From Cincinnati to Manchester: Pochettino in a hurry to paint town red
items.author: Barry Glendenning
items.content:
With his team mired in the relegation zone and a massive match at Liverpool this weekend, Mauricio Pochettino has been understandably busy since being appointed head coach of Manchester United. Unfortunately for Old Trafford regulars, the small print of his contract meant the Argentinian was tied up masterminding victory for USA USA USA in the second leg of their Concacaf Nations League quarter-final against Haiti when he ought to have been in Carrington moving red magnets around a tactics board in front of Marcus Rashford, Kobbie Mainoo and Harry Maguire.

items.content:
• Teenager says ‘thank you for everything’ in video

  • Gabriel expected to join Real Madrid

JJ Gabriel has announced his departure from Manchester United by posting a farewell message to the club on social media.

The teenager, who has not played a competitive game for the first team, joined as a 10-year-old in 2020 but has been absent since he requested the cancellation of his registration in September before he turned 16, on 6 October.

items.author: Press Association
items.content:
• Former England footballer opens up on mental health

  • ‘It was probably the lowest point’ at Manchester United

Wayne Rooney has revealed there was a period in his Manchester United career where he contemplated taking his own life. The former England striker said that, even as he flourished on the pitch, he was struggling with his mental health off it, despite being newly married and a dad to his eldest child, Kai.

items.title: Pochettino: I’d tell Guardiola to ‘take it’ if he’s offered US coaching job
items.author: Pablo Iglesias Maurer in Cincinnati and Jeff Rueter
items.content:
As he prepares to depart for Manchester United, the outgoing US coach held court on a number of topics, including what he’d change about soccer in America

Outgoing US head coach Mauricio Pochettino and former Manchester City head coach Pep Guardiola have a long, storied past. The two faced each other as players, when Guardiola was at Barcelona and Pochettino was making his name across town at Espanyol. They faced each other 22 times as managers in the Premier League and the two share a mutual respect – and intensity – when it comes to their approach to playing and coaching alike.

So when Guardiola visited Yankee Stadium in September to serve as New York City FC’s pre-match hype man before their rivalry match with Red Bull New York, Pochettino – in town anyways to scout the match – made it a point to sit with him during the game. He brought along his assistant coach and confidant Jesús Pérez, and US Soccer CEO and secretary general JT Batson.

items.title: Pulisic double leads US to 6-0 rout of Haiti in Pochettino’s farewell tour
items.author: Jeff Rueter
items.content:
• US take 6-0 lead in Nations League quarter-final

  • Hall, 18, scores again as Pochettino prepares for exit

  • Pulisic goes into fourth on all-time US scoring list

When Mauricio Pochettino named his US roster for the November window, few could have expected that the games would double as his brief lame-duck era. A week of camp instead brought constant media coverage, efficient negotiations and questions about the future of the national team. Come Wednesday, his day job will take him far from the federation’s headquarters in Fayetteville, Georgia, as he hopes to make sense of Manchester United.

Saturday finally allowed Pochettino and his players to get on with the intended purpose of this window, and they took to the Concacaf Nations League quarter-finals with aplomb. The US opened their two-leg series against Haiti with a dominant 6-0 victory in front of a considerably pro-Haitian crowd in Miami. Auston Trusty provided the first half’s only goal before Julian Hall, Christian Pulisic, Weston McKennie and Folarin Balogun contributed to the eventual rout.

items.title: Here Manchester United go again, taking the Two Ronnies route to hiring a new boss | Jonathan Wilson
items.author: Jonathan Wilson
items.content:
Mauricio Pochettino’s arrival feels like yet another appointment that would have been better made a few years ago

Magnusson: And your time starts … now! What is paleontology? Smithers: Yes, absolutely correct. Magnusson: What’s the name of the directory that lists members of the peerage? Smithers: A study of old fossils. Magnusson: Correct. Who are Len Murray and Sir Geoffrey Howe? Smithers: Burke’s. Magnusson: Correct. What is the difference between a donkey and an ass? Smithers: One’s a trade union leader, the other’s a member of the Cabinet …

One of the Two Ronnies’ most celebrated sketches involves a Mastermind contestant whose specialist subject is answering the previous question. History repeats itself: the first time as comedy, the second time as Manchester United, who seem continually to be answering not the question of who would be the best available manager now, but who might have been the best available manager a few years ago.

items.title: Tearful Pochettino says United job was ‘difficult to turn down’ in USMNT farewell
items.author: Pablo Iglesias Maurer in Fayetteville, Georgia
items.content:
• Coach was ‘transparent’ in dealings with club, federation

  • Pochettino had signed deal to stay with US through 2030

There were always going to be tears at Mauricio Pochettino’s news conference at US Soccer’s national training center on Friday. It was only a matter of when. Pochettino is famously emotional, and nobody in attendance had to wait long for the waterworks – they came during his introductory remarks, as he thanked the US Soccer executives flanking him for the opportunity to guide the US men. He grew emotional again as he addressed his impending departure for Manchester United, one announced just hours earlier.

“I think [the decision was],” Pochettino said, pausing to compose himself, “one of the most difficult decisions of our careers. Thank you guys. Thank you so much.”

Continue reading...

items.title: Mauricio Pochettino’s switch from USA to Manchester United confirmed
items.author: Pablo Iglesias Maurer and Will Unwin
items.content:
• Pochettino to take charge of two final USMNT matches

  • He has signed two-and-a-half-year United contract

Mauricio Pochettino’s switch from the US men’s national team to Manchester United has been confirmed. Pochettino will guide the US through a pair of Concacaf Nations League matches on Saturday and Tuesday before joining United, for whom his first game will come at Liverpool next Sunday.

The former Chelsea, Tottenham and Southampton manager has signed a two-and-a-half-year deal to replace Michael Carrick, who was sacked on Thursday after leading United to their worst start to a season in four decades. United have won one of their past 11 games and are in the Premier League’s relegation zone.

items.title: ‘United is broken’: Guardian readers react to Michael Carrick’s sacking
items.author: Guardian sport
items.content:
Emotions are running high after the confirmation of Michael Carrick’s dismissal at Old Trafford. Here are some views from our readers

“As a United fan who was around for the early 90s seeing Carrick go is a sad end to a horrible situation. He was the only likable thing about the club … I took my eight-year-old lad to Old Trafford for the Brighton game in the FA Cup in January and I’ve never experienced a more toxic atmosphere at a football ground. The fans deserve better … Better owners, better attitudes, better standards. Nothing will change with the setup of the club today and we are in this macabre holding pattern of failure, hope, anger and disappointment” –

“Wilcox, [Berada] and [Jim] Ratcliffe should have fired themselves. They are the common denominator of all this failure. [Mauricio] Pochettino will last 12 months if he’s lucky” –

items.title: Pochettino’s Chelsea maelstrom the best yardstick for what lies ahead at United
items.author: Andrew Beasley
items.content:
Argentinian oversaw high-scoring games in his one Chelsea season and Opta predicts his Manchester United side will move upfield quicker than that team

Among the 20 managers with more than 290 matches in the Premier League, only the five “big beasts” of Alex Ferguson, Arsène Wenger, José Mourinho, Jürgen Klopp and Pep Guardiola have better points-per-game averages than Mauricio Pochettino. He is an elite manager.

Pochettino took over Southampton midway through their first season back in the top flight (2012-13) after the club spent seven years in the lower leagues. In his only full campaign, they finished eighth. He led Tottenham to second in 2016-17, third in the seasons either side, and reached the 2019 Champions League final. His presence lifted those clubs.

items.title: Carrick sacked by Manchester United with team in Premier League relegation zone – as it happened
items.author: John Brewin; Luke McLaughlin and John Ashdown
items.content:
The latest news and reaction as Manchester United look for a new head coach after only only three victories so far this season

“After going through the Moyes season,” writes Hugh, “the dross football of Mourinho and Van Gaal, the moments-years of Solskjaer, the Rangnick surgery that never was, the middling Ten Hag, the baffling Amorim, and now a decent man thrust into the meat grinder, this is the first year it’s been genuinely hard to watch Man Utd with any emotion.

“And it’s not because of the football. It’s that the Glazer ownership and Ratcliffe mismanagement has met the Man City revelations, meaning it’s hard to see the point anymore. £1bn taken out of the club while others were illicitly pumping in roughly the same. A club drained of life, hollowed out … I can take crap football, but I can’t take this anymore.”
